newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Bayer eyes record full year profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bayer eyes record full year profit.

text.p: Strong nine-month results, fuelled largely by acquisitions, put Germany's Bayer AG on track for a record full year profit and probably a higher dividend, the company said on Tuesday.
"I can assure you 1996 will be a record year for Bayer," chief executive Manfred Schneider told a news conference.
He forecast the chemical and drugs group's full year sales would rise six percent to 47 billion marks ($31.06 billion) while net profits would jump 10 percent to 2.6 billion marks.
In the first nine months it reported a 12 percent rise in group pre-tax earnings to 3.7 billion marks with net profit climbing 18 percent to 2.3 billion marks.
Sales, driven largely by acquisitions and higher turnover in North America, climbed 7.4 percent to 36.5 billion marks.
The results largely met analysts' forecasts but did not fully satisfy Bayer, Schneider said. He noted business in Europe, particularly in Germany, was especially weak.
"Growth came entirely from a nine percent rise in foreign sales and domestic sales were two percent lower than a year ago, which was obviously disappointing," Schneider said.
But with Bayer poised to set record results for the second year, shareholders will likely profit.

"Judging by the past years when we have always had a dynamic dividend policy, we see no reason to expect a negative trend this year, and the trend will likely not be static either," Schneider told reporters.
Analysts were pleased that Bayer now enjoys a lower tax rate. That prompted BHF Bank in Frankfurt to raise its 1996 earnings per share estimate to 4.05 marks from 3.90 marks per share.
In the fourth quarter, however, Bayer said additional charges for early retirement at its Agfa unit as well as restructuring costs will weigh on results.
The single largest growth component were the acquisitions of the ABS plastics, printing plate, and Florasynth fragrance groups, Schneider said.

A 19.4 percent rise in sales in North America to 9.05 billion marks also fuelled growth. The trend of strong foreign growth is expected to continue as sluggish European economic conditions show few signs of improving soon, Schneider added.
Developments in Latin America and Asia were also strong, even though the weaker yen and some drug price cuts in Japan weighed on sales in Asia.

Eyeing the Asian market's growth potential, Bayer said it plans to invest 1.5 billion marks in the region in the next four to five years, entering joint-ventures in China and building new plants in Indonesia and Singapore.

In its biggest single business unit, health care, Bayer reported a 3.7 percent jump to 8.67 billion marks. Its Glucobay diabetes drug and genetically engineered Factor VIII blood clotting product Kogenate posted growth of over 50 percent.

Long praised for its strong drugs pipeline, Bayer said it expected to launch a new cholesterol reducing product called Cerivastatin, with an estimated sales potential of 700 million mark, in the next few months.

It also laid to rest speculation that may follow rival Hoechst AG's plans to separate its drugs business into a separate legal entity. "For the time the drugs unit is staying with us," Schneider said.
But Schneider added Bayer remains interested in forming cooperations and taking stakes in companies to boost its position, even though these would not be major takeovers.
Several acquistions are likely to be announced before the end of the year, Schneider said.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($1=1.5129 Mark)
